summary: DAY expectations/execution reviewed all 12 active-batch names while preserving the Earth-Score/opportunity firewall. Operating evidence is strong across much of the batch, but this pass did not obtain a single consistent same-timestamp market-price/consensus dataset for all 12. Therefore no current valuation bands, Opportunity Scores or Action States are invented. The execution conclusion is uniformly conservative: strong operating momentum may already embed demanding expectations, and correlated AI-capex exposure must be measured before deployment logic can be trusted.

companies.expectationTest: Record revenue/backlog plus Iridium/Motiv/Mynaric expansion raise the operating ceiling, but execution depends on Neutron and acquisition integration. Without same-timestamp market value and diluted-capital bridge, reward/risk cannot be quantified.
unknowns: current fully diluted market cap, consensus revenue/EBITDA bridge
companies.falsifier: if valuation already discounts flawless Neutron and integration, execution attractiveness can be poor despite strong Earth thesis

companies.expectationTest: Hypergrowth connectivity economics can command extreme multiples; end-customer concentration and insourcing risk must be incorporated before an opportunity premium is justified.
unknowns: current valuation, forward consensus and acquisition cash bridge
companies.falsifier: high multiple plus slowing program diversification would create narrative/valuation compression even if revenue still grows

companies.expectationTest: 104% YoY revenue growth and an accelerated Scorpio ramp support exceptional operating momentum, but such acceleration likely raises the expectations hurdle; warrant/customer concentration must be normalized before valuation is actionable.
unknowns: same-timestamp enterprise value and consensus ramp assumptions
companies.falsifier: deceleration from expected Scorpio ramp would be disproportionately damaging if valuation assumes sustained triple-digit growth

companies.expectationTest: Platform leadership is strong, but execution attractiveness depends on how much sustained hyperscaler capex and export-policy resilience are already priced. No current valuation/consensus precision is assumed.
unknowns: current consensus growth/margin path and implied terminal expectations
companies.falsifier: earnings growth can remain positive while multiple compresses if expectations outrun incremental demand

companies.expectationTest: Q2 revenue +50% and data-center +107% support a rising execution trajectory, but announced gigawatt-scale deployments must convert into durable share and gross profit to justify elevated expectations.
unknowns: current valuation and market-implied accelerator-share path
companies.falsifier: deployment announcements convert slower than expected or require margin sacrifice

companies.expectationTest: AI revenue acceleration and VMware cash generation are powerful, but custom-silicon concentration plus residual debt/tax tails make downside nonlinear if a major AI customer pauses.
unknowns: current valuation and customer-specific revenue concentration
companies.falsifier: a concentrated customer/program loss would expose whether valuation assumes uninterrupted AI growth

companies.expectationTest: Q2 revenue +36% and 67.7% gross margin show extraordinary operating power; execution must still price geopolitical tail risk, overseas-capacity returns and customer concentration rather than treating quality as sufficient.
unknowns: same-timestamp valuation and normalized overseas-fab margin drag
companies.falsifier: capital intensity rises while overseas returns lag and valuation still prices peak margins

companies.expectationTest: Raised 2026 guidance and High-NA adoption support premium quality, but monopoly scarcity can produce a priced-for-perfection setup when export/supplier risks remain asymmetric.
unknowns: current valuation and consensus High-NA ramp assumptions
companies.falsifier: bookings/shipments remain strong but multiple contracts as export/supplier risk reprices

companies.expectationTest: Direct silicon optionality could expand revenue, but market expectations may capitalize a much larger TAM before economics are proven. Governance/control complexity adds an execution discount that should not be ignored.
unknowns: current valuation, related-party economics and silicon gross-margin profile
companies.falsifier: direct silicon fails to produce attractive incremental returns or damages licensee growth

companies.expectationTest: HBM4 production validates a premium product cycle, but memory execution requires separating structural AI demand from cyclical peak pricing and supply response.
unknowns: current valuation, normalized mid-cycle earnings and debt/capex bridge
companies.falsifier: HBM gross-margin premium compresses faster than capex falls

companies.expectationTest: 35% Q1 growth and AI-networking architecture breadth support execution, but a concentrated hyperscaler customer set and white-box/custom alternatives can create valuation asymmetry.
unknowns: current valuation and latest customer concentration
companies.falsifier: growth decelerates before diversification broadens while valuation assumes sustained AI-networking share gains

companies.expectationTest: Record backlog/orders and stronger balance-sheet structure support execution credibility, but 2.9x book-to-bill may already imply a steep future conversion curve that is vulnerable to hyperscaler schedule changes.
unknowns: current valuation, customer concentration and cancellation terms
companies.falsifier: backlog conversion slows while valuation assumes full near-term realization

contradictions: Business quality and operating momentum are exceptionally strong across several names, but that is not equivalent to attractive execution when valuation/consensus inputs are absent.
The batch is heavily correlated to the same AI infrastructure capex pool, so independent company theses can still share one macro execution failure mode.
Backlog and design-win evidence are leading indicators, not realized cash flow or guaranteed margin.
unknowns: No consistent same-timestamp price/enterprise-value/consensus dataset was acquired for all 12 names in this pass.
Opportunity Score and Action State therefore remain intentionally unset for the batch.
Crowding, factor correlation and option-implied event risk were not measured with primary/reliable market data.
